dedupe_keys.name: zero emission grid rest gis mapping tool for data centre and large load site selection

description: REST is a commercial GIS mapping tool from Zero-Emission Grid (ZEG), a US consultancy on grid interconnection, which ZEG markets for screening sites for data centres, energy storage, generation and other large loads. A ZEG guide dated 9 September 2025 describes how the tool evaluates power access and cost, fibre resilience, land developability, hazards and long-term operating economics in one workflow: users look at proximity to transmission lines and substations, likely interconnection congestion and queue wait times, nearby fibre routes and gas pipelines, buildable land and natural hazards, then shortlist and compare candidate sites. ZEG pairs the tool with services for site prospecting, multi-scenario analysis, interconnection queue insights and grid due diligence across the US market regions (CAISO, ERCOT, ISO-NE, MISO, NYISO, PJM and SPP), and also offers a Sitra product and a free GridLens tool. Coverage: the United States. Format and access: web-based commercial software; walkthroughs and pricing on request. Caveats: proprietary, with data sources and update schedules not published on the page read; the guide is marketing material. Simulation uses: siting of new data centres against grid capacity, fibre diversity and hazard exposure, and screening interdependency risks between data centres and the power grid. Related records: Land id is a comparable parcel-mapping tool, and the IM3 open-source data center atlas and EPRI load projections cover data centre locations and demand.
